The core insight emerges from the interplay between experimental design and motivational hierarchy. The obstruction method serves as a proxy for quantifying animal motivation by observing behavioral responses to varying goal objects. This leads to a structured ordinal ranking of drives, which can be modeled as a preference kernel in GSI's Bayesian framework. The consistency of these rankings across different apparatus types suggests a universal motivational structure. In GSE, this translates into a dynamic state transition model where each goal object corresponds to a node in a motivational graph. The failure mode occurs when environmental novelty or stress disrupts the established hierarchy, leading to non-monotonic behavior. The mathematical duality lies in treating motivation as both a scalar (intensity) and vector (directionality) field, enabling robust inference under uncertainty.
